overview: The commission approved field use applications for youth softball and the American Cancer Society's Relay for Life, and authorized the installation of a Blue Bike station. Discussion also covered stadium maintenance, including press box repairs and a recent deep cleaning of the turf.

items.title: Medford Youth Girls Softball Application
items.summary: Approved the field use application for Medford Youth Girls Softball, with the understanding that they will coordinate scheduling with Medford Baseball for Drain Field 1.

items.title: American Cancer Society Relay for Life
items.summary: Approved the application for the Relay for Life event on June 10, provided that food and staging are kept off the synthetic turf and noise levels are managed after 9:00 p.m.

items.title: Blue Bike Station Installation
items.summary: Approved the installation of a Blue Bike station at Hormel Stadium following a review of the location and logistics.

items.title: Memorial Plaque Dedication
items.summary: Reviewed the completed Karasiewicz memorial plaque and discussed a potential dedication ceremony during the fifth-grade Junior Olympics on June 2.

items.title: Financial and Maintenance Updates
items.summary: Recreation Director Kevin Bailey reported a $25,000 discrepancy between department records and the finance office and noted that the press box requires approximately $4,000 in siding and roof repairs. The commission also noted the completion of a professional $2,850 deep cleaning and magnetic sweep of the turf field.

items.title: Event Vetting and Rental Policy
items.summary: Discussed establishing stricter guidelines and higher rental rates for non-athletic festivals to mitigate issues with trash, noise, and damage to the synthetic turf.
